sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Brings in column types, the enum tool, the link to the shared base and the portable UUID type.
sections.why: Likely reason: the User class and role list need these tools.
sections.watch_out: The Enum type is imported but not used for the role column.

sections.name: UserRole
sections.title: Access role names
sections.what: Lists the three roles: Consultant, Reviewer and Admin.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed set of roles that permission rules refer to.
sections.watch_out: The labels are capitalized, so checks must use the exact spelling.

sections.name: User
sections.title: User account record
sections.what: Defines the account table with email, hashed password, name, role, active flag, timestamps, last sign in and links to projects and audit entries.
sections.why: Likely reason: identifies each person and what they may do.
sections.watch_out: The model only stores is_active. Code must check it, or disabled accounts can still sign in.

summary: Defines the user account table and the three roles that control access.
purpose: Stores who can sign in, their role, password hash and login times, and links each user to their projects and audit entries.
why: Likely reason: access rules need a user identity and a role to check against.
how: 1) The role list names Consultant, Reviewer and Admin. 2) The user record holds email, hashed password, name, role, active flag, timestamps and last login. 3) Links connect each user to their projects and audit entries.
inputs: User records created on sign up or by the development path in the project route.
risks: Role is stored as plain text, so a typo is accepted. This file does not create password hashes. The email must be unique.
debug: If sign in fails, check is_active and hashed_password. If a user cannot create projects, check their role.
